title: Granular trace hooks and noise-aware alert attunement
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Enable fine-grained trace hook instrumentation and an adaptive alerting layer that reduces pager noise while preserving SLO fidelity. This ticket coordinates instrumentation changes across the runtime and API edge to emit lightweight start/end span hooks, enrich traces with routing and model-variant metadata, and feed a denoising pipeline that improves burn-rate and anomaly signals. Goals: (1) add low-overhead hook points in the serving runtime and SDKs, (2) create a streaming enrichment pipeline to join traces with metrics/logs, (3) implement a noise-aware scoring layer for alerts so we reduce false positive paging for transient tail latencies, and (4) ship dashboards and runbooks for oncall. Constraints: minimal latency overhead (<0.25ms p50), limited retention change, keep changes deployable to Dedicated and Private without config drift.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits new start/end hooks with <0.25ms median overhead in microbenchmark
Enrichment pipeline joins traces to per-request metric buckets and model-variant tags in near real-time (<5s processing lag)
Alert scoring reduces repeat paging on transient spikes by >=40% in the staged region without missing sustained SLO violations
New latency/error dashboards show per-model variant baselines and a denoised burn-rate visualization; runbook published and reviewed by SRE
tasks: Design trace hook API and versioned spec (runtime + SDKs)
Implement non-blocking hook points at request start/end and kv-cache boundaries
Add model_variant and route metadata to span attributes
Build streaming enrichment job (Kafka -> Flink/Beam) to join metrics/logs/traces
Develop alert scoring microservice that ingests enriched signals and outputs adjusted burn-rate signals
Create Grafana dashboards and lightweight runbook pages for paging policy changes
Staged rollout on canary region, A/B compare alert noise and detection recall
progress_updates: 2026-02-20 - Ticket created by Marco Ruiz: initial scope and goals. Asked for SRE and SDK owners to review.
2026-02-25 - Design review: agreed to use versioned hook spec to avoid breaking Dedicated/Private customers. Action: publish spec draft on Confluence.
2026-03-01 - Prototype: added start/end hook in runtime; benchmark shows 0.18ms median overhead (good). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4021
2026-03-04 - Trade-off discussion: SRE recommended incremental enrichment (metrics-first join) to limit pipeline state size. Decided to implement a lightweight sharded join keyed by request_id.
2026-03-08 - Alert scoring prototype implemented; reproducible test shows 45% reduction in duplicate pages on synthetic spike. Need to validate recall on historical incidents.
2026-03-12 - Preparing canary: dashboards wired and runbook drafted. Requesting SRE approval for canary start next week.
Pending - follow-up: tie into rollout policy to disable scoring per-customer if regulatory customers request raw signals
decisions: Use start/end trace hooks only (avoid per-token hooks) to keep overhead minimal
Version the trace-hook API so Dedicated/Private installs can opt-in to new hook schema
Enrichment pipeline chooses metrics-first streaming join to bound memory footprint
Alert scoring uses a two-stage approach: statistical denoising (IQR-based) then model-based anomaly scorer for persistent shifts
Keep raw unadjusted alerts available for audit; scoring produces secondary adjusted signal used for paging decisions
Do not change default retention in this ticket; longer retention work to be tracked separately
risks: Incorrect join keys could cause missing context leading to worse SLO signal quality
Over-aggressive denoising might suppress real regressions during slow ramp events
Deployment differences across Private customers could cause inconsistent observability if they don't opt into hooks
Pipeline operational complexity (stateful joins) may increase maintenance overhead for infra team
